neighbours.label: the equative 'as ... as': ' as' or ' much' / ' many' in 'as much as', 'as many ... as', 'as good as'
fire: Prices fell by as much as 40 per cent.
There are as many theories as there are authors.
The speed is as impressive as the range.
It fell by as much as half.
She is as tall as her brother.
It was as good as new.
The firm has as many staff as its rival.
quiet: Prices fell by more than 40 per cent.
There are many theories and many authors.
The speed is more impressive than the range.
She is taller than her brother.
The firm has more staff than its rival.

notes: The + pole of this neuron fires before comparatives (' than', ' better', ' worse'), so 'as ... as' against 'more ... than' looks like the distinction. 'more ... than' near misses reached 0.18 in probes.
